0.comment: Xilonen: Tumaini, the Traveler's Ancient Name
0.content:
In 5.0, after the Traveler helped rescue Kachina, Mavuika promised them an Ancient Name and handed the job to Xilonen, telling her only that it would be for "a traveler" and "quite difficult". In 5.1 Xilonen discovered the recipient was an outlander. The Night Kingdom records only Natlanese deeds, so a Name seemed impossible, but she took the task as proof of Mavuika's trust and a test of her own skill. She wrote to Citlali, and the two took the problem to the Lord of the Night, who created the Pilgrim's Chronicle to record the Traveler's deeds in Natlan. In the 5.2 Interlude Xilonen gathered people's stories of the Traveler before the Chronicle, with Paimon finishing it; in 5.3 she forged the Name within the three days before Mavuika's planned descent. It is Tumaini, "hope", the first ever borne by an outlander.

She skipped the usual Ley Line extraction ceremony because the Chronicle already held the memories, and gave the Chronicle back as "the most significant proof of your adventures in Natlan". After a barbecue dinner (her favourite place, which also has top-tier alcohol, to Citlali's interest) she tested the Name outside the Children of Echoes' camp. The Traveler's soul was so strong that it drew in wandering souls, and the group helped Citlali send them to rest. She told the Traveler to give the Name to Mavuika so the Archon could explain it to the people. In the final battle, the messages forged into Tumaini proved crucial; afterwards she called it "a perfect fit".

Separately, after Tlazolli could no longer make the Blazegem Inscription she had promised the Traveler, Xilonen offered to forge one herself. The Name holds everyone's blessing, she said; this would hold hers, and the Traveler may choose the words.

1.comment: Xilonen: The Price of Forging a Name
1.content:
That night in 5.1, Xilonen and Citlali visited the Lord of the Night. Asked whether the Traveler deserved a Name, Xilonen said they were special, had saved Kachina, and that Natlan owed them a debt a Name could at least protect. The Lord asked if she would pay with her own life. She said yes. The Lord explained that a new Name is like a seed and the Engraver's life is the outer shell that shields it until it takes root in the Night Kingdom, then gradually disappears. Xilonen called the sacrifice "practically negligible" if it gave Natlan a future, and said she would not regret it: "I bear the name 'Baraka.' This is a part of my duty."

In the same audience, Citlali revealed she had foreseen Mavuika's death, and the Lord of the Night confirmed that the price of Ronova's power is death. When the Traveler later asked what the Chronicle had cost, both women steered the talk to the Lord's generosity. Canon never states how much of Xilonen's life was spent, and shows no ill effect on her as of 7.1.

2.content:
Mavuika considers Xilonen one of the best craftsmen in Natlan, "well-versed in Secret Source technology", and admires that she never backs away from a challenge. Xilonen's view of their dealings: "ridiculous commissions." Mavuika wanted a sword that would not melt in her flames, sunglasses to see enemies through fire, and above all a phlogiston-powered vehicle. She kept showing up with dragon design schematics of unknown origin until Xilonen gave in. The Flamestrider took three whole months. Compared with all that, Xilonen says, an Ancient Name for an outlander was "a relatively reasonable task".

Xilonen refused to ride along during testing, claiming she had forgotten to make a second helmet; she told Mavuika it was fine, since "it's not like you're made of glass". In the 5.7 Anecdote "Xilonen: Face to Face" she tried to return a commission letter unopened, insisting clients talk face to face; when the letter said Mavuika was already waiting in her workshop to do exactly that, she fled. On one birthday Mavuika kicked down her door to drag her out of bed. She tells the Traveler the "glorious, righteous leader" is only one side of Mavuika, who can be "quite terrible 'sometimes'".

In 5.3, after Natlan's victory, Mavuika tracked her down napping (Ororon had given her away) to tell her that Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, was returning. Xilonen asked whether Mavuika was nervous to have someone show up "who could bring you down a notch", said she was starting to like the new Pilgrimage, and went back to sleep. Mavuika keeps planning Flamestrider upgrades to discuss with her.

3.content:
Teyiz was a renowned, kindly Name Engraver who taught the Children of Echoes' children. Xilonen was her one student who stayed awake through technical classes, firing off questions about phlogiston (could you cook meat by dropping it down a phlogiston-filled chimney?). She skipped the hero-story classes with excuses. Teyiz saw through them and told her that for Name Engravers, stories and equations are one and the same. In story classes Teyiz asked how an Engraver would choose between conflicting versions of a legend, and set the children to trace evidence across records. That approach won Xilonen over.

In old age Teyiz said she heard the Wayob calling but would stay until she had passed on what she must. After her funeral, rumours painted her as a saint or as a schemer who had misled children. Xilonen tracked down every trace of her across all six tribes to record the truth, then forged that truth into her own first Ancient Name, holding the comb Teyiz had used to coax her back to study. Who the Name would go to, she decided, was "the Wayob's concern, not hers". She received her Vision that same day without noticing.

4.content:
Tlazolli, bearer of the Ancient Name Undugu, was a celebrated Name Engraver Xilonen grew up admiring and calls "Auntie". Her daughter Nechca died in an Abyss attack years ago. Tlazolli took in Nepecha, an orphan from the same attack born on the same day, and passed her off as Nechca recovering from illness and memory loss. Xilonen, who thought of herself as Nechca's pen-pal big sister, visited with a book Nechca had asked for. She found that Tlazolli's popular Blazegem Inscriptions were near-Ancient Names secretly draining the tribe's memories of Nechca. Tlazolli meant to overwrite Nepecha's mind with them.

Xilonen took apart the Central Inscription Tlazolli gave her, aware that she too might be a target. She followed Tlazolli to her supposedly closed forge, struck a flaw in the engraving diagram on the count of three, and confronted her. The figures Tlazolli had summoned were only the grief people felt beside a dying child, Xilonen told her; the real Nechca had always been recorded in Tlazolli's own Name, the one she had called useless. "Names are blessings from the past to the future... You told me that, Auntie." Nechca's spirit spoke to them one last time. Xilonen tied Tlazolli up and handed her to the tribe. Her punishment was undecided, since almost no one had used an Ancient Name for a crime before.

The Inscriptions were destroyed and the stolen memories returned. Xilonen gave Nepecha a stone engraved with her real name, took her into her workshop, began an official investigation into her past and started teaching her crafting. Nepecha keeps a diary, wants to become a Name Engraver, and in 5.3 asked Xilonen to take her to bless the Traveler before the final battle.

5.comment: Xilonen: Ancient Names and the Name Engraver's craft
5.content:
Ancient Names carry past heroes' legacies. Each comes as a feather-shaped obsidian stone, and the Wayob grant them to those who have "done something in their lifetime that exemplifies the 'spirit' of the Name." The Children of Echoes believe only their tribe can bear the duty of forging them. Xilonen says the technique is simple; the hard part is verifying deeds whose witnesses are long dead. She uses the Masters of the Night-Wind's woven scrolls, Citlali's knowledge and contacts across the six tribes, cross-referencing every link. A falsehood makes a Name "seriously defective" and can cause cognitive problems for its bearer. Names can also be forged from a deserving person's life after death, and the Wayob choose who receives them.

Her own Name, Baraka ("blessing"), was first borne by Ixquieh, founder of the Children of Echoes and one of Xbalanque's Six Heroes. As a modern Baraka bearer she was one of three heroes already acknowledged when the Traveler arrived (with Kinich and Iansan). With Mualani, Ororon and Chasca they completed the six whose Names helped Mavuika end the war. Most of Xilonen's work is not Names at all but tools and weapons for her tribe.

6.content:
Citlali comes to the workshop to buy ore she grinds into medicine for divinations. Xilonen has never wanted her own fortune read and admits divination rituals make her sleepy. Citlali likes her because she ignores the rumours and is not overly friendly. Xilonen admitted she "forgot to mention" to the Traveler that the "Granny" is actually young. The two co-led the work on the Traveler's Name, shared the secret of its price and of Mavuika's foretold death, and in 5.3 guided wandering souls together. Xilonen teased her for making things dramatic because of "all those novels you read".

In 5.8 they briefly disagreed over Ineffa: Citlali feared her core might be a hostile Sovereign Lord, while Xilonen felt a technician's duty to repair her. They argued, then examined her together.

7.comment: Xilonen: Kachina and the Children of Echoes
7.content:
The Children of Echoes are miners, gem appraisers and smiths in the gorges of Tequemecan Valley. Xilonen's workshop sits near the settlement, and the red cliffs make her feel at home in a way the other tribes do not. After Kachina received her Ancient Name, Chief Pacal brought her to Xilonen for a drill. Xilonen built Turbo Twirly, dropped the seat for a manual control system at Kachina's request, and removed shock absorption because Kachina wanted direct feedback; now she wonders about mouthguards. The two admire each other's gem collections. In 5.1, when the Abyss invaded, Pacal ordered the tribe evacuated while Kachina and Xilonen held the rear and destroyed Abyssal Pylons near the settlement.

In the 2025 birthday letter, Kachina once sat outside Xilonen's door with a gift from morning to sunset because Xilonen was asleep. Xilonen then built a "birthday alarm clock" that rings only on her birthday, and on a later birthday the two made candies together.

8.content:
- Chasca: a gun for high-altitude combat, needing special ammunition, recoil and accuracy fixes. Chasca said basic crosshairs were enough. Xilonen questioned her for a day and made her learn a maintenance guide; Chasca suspects it was really so she would fly safe.
- Mualani: the shark surfboard; Xilonen has never seen her slip on a Spiritway.
- Iansan: super-heavy plates and dumbbells for the Collective of Plenty, which Iansan loaded into a cart one by one, barely winded.
- Ifa: Saurian syringes so imposing that patients behave even without the needle; she offers to show you the biggest.
- Kinich: answering her job posting for a hardy, low-maintenance plant, he brought Saurian claw succulent seeds; not one sprouted. She wonders whether Ajaw, if he came from a device, could be made to shut up for good.

9.comment: Xilonen: The Abyss Invasion and Capitano
9.content:
When Capitano and Ororon tried to rebuild Natlan's Ley Lines with a Secret Source device, Mavuika led Xilonen, Kinich and the Traveler against his base. Xilonen tunnelled the party in while Kinich drew off the Fatui. Ororon, briefly possessed, lunged at her before Capitano restrained him. When the Lord of the Night offered to rebuild the Ley Lines at the cost of herself and Natlan's history, Xilonen sided with Ororon and Mavuika: life must have meaning. Then the Abyss struck nationwide. She fought Abyssal Pylons, evacuated her tribe to the Stadium, and admitted she had never believed the old stories of a blackened sky until she saw it. "As long as there's even a sliver of hope, I'm not gonna give up." When Mavuika declared a Night Warden War, Xilonen spoke her tribe's invocation: "Stone engraved and echoing peaks. Converge, disperse, in ashes be reborn."

At the victory feast she proposed a moment of silence for the fallen. Testing Tumaini in 5.3, she struck down the soul of a man named Zumalli when the Abyss began corrupting it, because sending him to the Night Kingdom would only spread the damage. She respected two Tepetlisaur souls who chose to stay with their grandson Ayo. She saw that Capitano truly wanted to help lost souls.

10.content: A woven scroll in Xilonen's workshop shows Ixquieh, first recorded bearer of Baraka, founder of the Children of Echoes and one of Xbalanque's Six Heroes in the war against the Pyro Dragon Xiuhcoatl. Xilonen explained in 5.8 that Ixquieh took apart many dragon machines hoping to use them for humanity. After their old friend Och-Kan became a tyrant who persecuted anything tied to dragonkind, Ixquieh burned her workshop so he could not use it, which is why most of her research is lost; Chasca's predecessor Lianca saved a little of it. Ixquieh's twin Ahpub founded the Collective of Plenty.

11.content: In the 5.8 Archon Quest prelude The Journey Home, Chasca and the Traveler brought an unconscious automaton woman and a cryptex to Xilonen, whom Mavuika had just tasked with the rogue Secret Source automatons. Xilonen found the cryptex built from many nations' materials and would not force it. The woman's core resembled a Secret Source core, but the rest was foreign (Fontainian clockwork joints, a Mondstadt-style maid's hairpiece); Xilonen woke her simply by stimulating the core, to her own surprise. She suspected an isolation block on her memories and had her tidy the workshop. Later Xilonen and Citlali privately feared the woman, Ineffa, might hold the Eleventh Sovereign Lord's core; Chasca refused to treat her as a threat. Xilonen helped stabilise collapsing ruins and later certified Ineffa in good working order. The cryptex held Varka's invitation for the Traveler to come to Nod-Krai.

12.comment: Xilonen: Legion of Soulblazers at Dragonspine (6.2 event)
12.content: During the limited-time 6.2 event Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey, Xilonen came to Dragonspine for the Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge. She represented Nepecha, a member of the Legion of Soulblazers (a comic-book fan club of pen pals devoted to The Soulblazer Saga), who was not fit for extreme sports. She ended up as vice captain beside Varesa, Minnie, Tang Yigang and Alrani, coached the team's running form, and ran the first relay leg when Yigang fell ill. She shopped for Soulblazer "merch" for Nepecha. Seeing that young Minnie's parents dismissed her art as wasted time, she spoke to them as Nepecha's teacher: she gave them a group painting by Nepecha and the Children of Echoes' children, and compared Minnie to a Mondstadt bard with an audience. She also napped on a library table.

13.comment: Xilonen: Music and the Dance-Off Stage
13.content: The Children of Echoes love rhythmic music, and their Drillbit Dance dance-off is held daily (the tribe's bulletin board numbers it in its 127,751st iteration, roughly 350 years). When the old Dance-Off Stage broke mid-contest, Xilonen rewired it, tested the mic and played a track that brought the crowd roaring back. She had picked up DJing while learning record pressing from the People of the Springs. She refused a paid post, maintains the stage for free, and wants to be its official DJ once she no longer has to forge Names. Her headphones link to a record player at the forge, she curated Muhuru's Gemporium's playlist (Varesa runs to it), and her combat gear includes a portable phlogiston DJ controller. In 6.5 she helped Barbara of Mondstadt adjust the rhythm of a hymn.

14.content: After the war, Xilonen can "head out whenever I feel like it". In the 6.5 Anecdote "Dahlia: Day of Confession", Barbara mistook her tail hanging from a tree outside Mondstadt for a wild beast; Xilonen, yawning throughout, helped her adjust a hymn. Her birthday letter of 2026-03-13 says she was in Liyue choosing ores and jewellery whose shopkeepers' backstories she doubted. She saw a man with an unusual sword board a ship for Inazuma and decided that would be her next stop.

15.content: During the limited-time 6.6 event Kaleidoscopic Color Chase, Minnie visited Natlan to meet Varesa, Xilonen and Nepecha; her parents had become less strict since the Dragonspine contest. After Nepecha spent time with Minnie, she suggested Mualani might invite Barbara (seen in Minnie's drawings) to her next dance party, and Xilonen agreed to show Mualani the drawings.
